title: Prevent tenant namespace drift during VPC peering churn by adding deterministic SNAT pools and coordinated conntrack flush
creator: Aisha Patel
description: High-priority production fix for intermittent tenant namespace drift observed during VPC peering churn on Dedicated clusters. Customer-facing symptom: tenant A observed occasional resolution and egress mapping to tenant B hostnames after peering reconciliation, causing cross-tenant request attribution and short-lived data-plane isolation breaches. This ticket scopes investigation, mitigation, and production rollout of deterministic per-tenant SNAT pools + controlled conntrack and DNS cache reconciliation to prevent future occurrences.
repro_steps: 1) Create two dedicated tenants with VPC peering between their egress subnets.
2) Drive heavy connect/disconnect churn (scale up/down or route re-parenting) on peering attachment to force ephemeral NAT port reuse and conntrack state reuse.
3) Observe that ephemeral source ports and stale conntrack entries sometimes map to the wrong tenant while DNS resolver caches still hold prior hostnames (TTL jitter).
4) Confirm cross-tenant hostname resolution or response attribution in packet captures and in per-tenant flow logs.
root_cause_summary: Race between peering route re-parenting, SNAT ephemeral port reuse, and DNS cache TTL misalignment caused short windows where egress flows retained conntrack bindings to the old egress identity while resolver caches still returned hostnames tied to a previous tenant. The combination of asynchronous control-plane reconciliation and lack of deterministic SNAT assignment allowed transient mapping of flows to incorrect tenant SNAT pools.
mitigation: Implemented deterministic per-tenant SNAT pools (tenant -> fixed ephemeral range) to eliminate ephemeral port overlap between tenants during scale/peering churn.
Added an orchestrated conntrack flush hook in the peering reconciliation sequence to clear stale 5-tuple state immediately after route swap completes.

Aligned resolver TTL behavior during peering events by adding a short-lived forced negative/refresh probe that truncates in-memory resolver TTLs for affected tenants for the first 60s post-switchover.
Added a temporary emergency firewall rule as a safeguard to drop flows that attempt to use SNAT ranges not assigned to the originating tenant while we roll out fixes.
fix_patch: Deterministic SNAT allocator + peering reconciler conntrack flush + resolver TTL refresh patch
deployment_plan: Canary deploy in us-west-2 on a small dedicated cluster with active customer traffic (week 1).
Monitor egress attribution, conntrack churn, and DNS-flap metrics for 48 hours; if stable, expand canary to 4 clusters (week 2).
Full rollout gated by health: no cross-tenant egress events and connection success rate within 0.1% of baseline for 72 hours.
If regression observed, automatic rollback to previous SNAT allocator and revert conntrack flush hook; notify on-call and begin warmfix cycle.
rollout_status: Completed: patched, canaryed, and fully rolled out across Dedicated clusters in us-west-2/us-east-1/eu-west-1
verification_checks: Synthetic egress tests that assert per-tenant source IP/port mapping post-peering-switchover
Flow logs correlation dashboard shows zero cross-tenant hostname mapping after rollout
Aggressive scale-up/down churn tests do not produce conntrack reuse across tenants
DNS resolver probe logs show TTL refresh events exactly during the 60s window post-switchover
